issues.legal_issue: An assignee may enforce a right of repurchase by specific performance when the contract does not make that right personal to the original holders.
material_facts: The original resale agreements granted the vendors a right to repurchase but did not state that the right was personal or nonassignable.
The vendors later entered agreements assigning their rights to the plaintiff, who paid consideration and received the original resale agreements.
The plaintiff sued for specific performance, joined the original vendors and the purchasers’ successors, and deposited the amounts due under the agreements.
The purchasers’ successors refused to execute the reconveyance deeds.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff was a representative in interest and could enforce the assigned repurchase rights by specific performance; the appeals were allowed and the trial court decrees restored.
issues.legal_principle: Section 15(b) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 permits specific performance to be obtained by a representative in interest. A repurchase right is generally assignable unless the contract shows that it was intended to be personal. The Court approved Sakalaguna v. Munnuswami, AIR 1928 PC 174; Vishweshwar v. Durgappa, AIR 1946 Bombay 339, including its discussion of Section 23(b) of the Specific Relief Act, 1877; and Sinnakaruppa v. Karuppuswami, AIR 1965 Madras 506.

rule.if: repurchase_contract_not_personal and repurchase_right_assigned and assignee_sued_for_specific_performance and assignee_ready_to_perform

predicates.repurchase_contract_not_personal: The contract granting a right to repurchase does not make that right personal to the original holder or prohibit its assignment.
predicates.repurchase_right_assigned: The original holder assigns the repurchase right to another person.
predicates.assignee_sued_for_specific_performance: The assignee brings a suit seeking specific performance of the assigned repurchase right.
predicates.assignee_ready_to_perform: The assignee demonstrates readiness and willingness to perform, including by depositing the amount due.
predicates.assignee_can_enforce_repurchase_right_by: The assignee is entitled to enforce the repurchase right by specific performance.

issues.definition: When a nonpersonal repurchase right is assigned, the assignee may enforce it by specific performance if the assignee sues for that relief and is ready to perform.

issues.legal_issue: A shorter period stated in an agreement between the original holder and an assignee does not defeat the assignee’s timely enforcement of an assigned repurchase right merely because the original contract allowed a longer period.
material_facts: The original repurchase agreements allowed the original holders to exercise their rights during a three-year window.
The later agreements with the plaintiff provided a two-year period for obtaining the sale deeds.
The plaintiff sought specific performance within the two-year period stated in the later agreements.
issues.conclusion: The shorter period did not deprive the plaintiff of the right to enforce the assigned repurchase agreements, because the plaintiff exercised that right within the stipulated two-year period.
issues.legal_principle: The Court interpreted the original repurchase agreements together with the later sale agreements and held that the difference between their enforcement periods did not take away the assignee’s right to sue when the assignee acted within the shorter period. The Court relied on the principles of assignability discussed in Sakalaguna v. Munnuswami, AIR 1928 PC 174; Vishweshwar v. Durgappa, AIR 1946 Bombay 339; and Sinnakaruppa v. Karuppuswami, AIR 1965 Madras 506.

rule.if: specific_performance_proceeding and repurchase_right_assigned and assigned_window_shorter_than_original_window and suit_within_assigned_window

predicates.specific_performance_proceeding: The assignee brings a proceeding seeking specific performance of a repurchase right.
predicates.repurchase_right_assigned: The original holder assigns the repurchase right to another person.
predicates.assigned_window_shorter_than_original_wi: The agreement with the assignee allows a shorter period for enforcement than the original repurchase contract allows.
predicates.suit_within_assigned_window: The assignee seeks enforcement within the period stated in the agreement with the assignee.
predicates.longer_original_window_does_not_bar_assi: The longer period in the original contract does not bar the assignee from enforcing the right within the shorter assigned period.

issues.definition: If an assignee seeks specific performance within the shorter period stated in the assignment, the longer period in the original contract does not by itself bar enforcement.
